mentions.name: Underscore
mentions.description: This project uses LLMs to generate procedural ambient music by writing actual SuperCollider synth source code rather than audio files, so the music runs live and can be embedded in and controlled in real time by software like games. The pipeline depends on prompt engineering, aesthetic curation, and a compiler with automatic repair in the agent loop when generated code doesn't build. It currently produces single-synth musical systems, with research underway on orchestrating multiple synths into fuller, evolving compositions with deep musical form and structure, aiming to make algorithmic music more accessible to artists.

mentions.name: Underscore
mentions.description: This web SDK and browser sandbox lets users build procedural music systems with LLMs. Instead of generating finished audio files, an LLM helps write and revise a SuperCollider-based system that runs in the browser via WebAssembly, yielding executable music that is inspectable, editable, versionable, and controllable at runtime. It targets adaptive sound for software such as games, creative tools, meditation apps, AI agents, and interactive art.
mentions.problem: Static audio files feel too dead for adaptive sound in software, and hiring a composer or sound designer for every variation is unrealistic.
mentions.audience: Builders of games, creative tools, meditation apps, AI agents, and interactive art looking for adaptive sound.
